newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to test $2,600, aluminium steady.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to test $2,600, aluminium steady.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are likely to tackle the $2,600 level on Tuesday, extending the previous session's upward momentum, analysts said.
But there could be a hurdle if LME stocks rise, following an increase overnight in Comex inventories.
Aluminium, meanwhile, is likely to remain stable some way adrift of $1,600 overhead.
Although the market is still overbought, with the momentum indicators continuing at percentage levels, copper probably has enough bullish sentiment in the short-term to offset that.
The backwardation remains around $95/100, basis cash/threes, and there is an undercurrent of potential supply shortages in Canada, Russia and Papua New Guinea.

"The technical picture also supports the tightening fundamentals as we look for further challenges of overhead resistance, with the formation of a potentially bullish flag pattern," said Martin Squires of LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co.
If so, the market is expected to re-challenge last week's 13-month high of $2,606 and then run up to test $2,650 on the charts, dealers said.
At 0741 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,599/604, up from Monday's late close of $2,597/600.
The scenario is different in aluminium where prices have not performed as well as copper even though inventory drawdowns are larger and more consistent.

"Chartwise, the market looks vulnerable to further declines...Support is seen in the first instance at $1,575, but if this level is breached the completion of a triple-top formation would target the $1,540/50 area," LME trader Brandeis said.
But in the short-term prices are likely to hold comfortably above $1,570/75, with copper at least providing some modest support, dealers said.
At 0741 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,588/90, up around $3.50 from yesterday's late close. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
